title: Semantic Tokens Source Editor UI
summary: Define catalogue discovery and creation before deriving token syntax, then define caret recognition, metadata editing, highlighting, and removal.
content_html:
Semantic Tokens Source Editor UI

Outcome

Make the UI the normal way to add and maintain semantic tokens. An author should not need to remember token syntax, manually edit ids, or discover required fields after insertion fails.

This is a manage-only feature hosted by the existing Markdown source editor, modal lifecycle, and Info panel. It does not add another editor or write path.

This workflow is accepted before token syntax and Architecture. It determines when meaning is chosen, what identity must be stored, and which data discovery must provide.

Responsibility Change From The Pilot

The pilot hosts target search, mixed-target results, target selection, and immediate token insertion in the Info panel. That proves the Info panel can host substantial manage-mode UI, but it is not the target responsibility split.

The new contract is:

surface responsibility
family-specific add modal search all accepted target types in the family, choose the concrete target identity, collect required occurrence data, and create the token
family-specific Info view inspect an existing occurrence, edit only its mutable occurrence fields, and display declared read-only usage or target-lookup context

Target search and identity selection exist only during creation. An Info view does not contain a target search control, a target result list, or any other control capable of changing the existing token's identity.

CT-P1 extracts the title-weighted search and keyboard-navigable result component from the pilot Info-panel view and hosts it in the Catalogue add modal. The mixed Work, Series, and Moment results remain. The pilot's Info-panel placement and immediate select-to-insert composition are retired.

Source-Mode States

The source editor has three relevant contextual states:

source state toolbar Info panel
no active token one add action per accepted family ordinary source/document information
caret inside a valid token add actions remain available matching family-specific token view
exact active-token range selected by the feature add actions remain available same token view remains active

Adding begins from a toolbar action and modal. Inspecting begins from the caret and never becomes another route into identity selection.

Add A Token

Each accepted family contributes one clearly named source-editor toolbar button. The first is Add catalogue token. Tags later receive Add tag token rather than being mixed into Catalogue discovery.

Clicking the button:

  1. captures the current selection text and range before focus moves;
  2. opens the family's add modal;
  3. prefills the title or equivalent field from the selected text;
  4. collects and validates every required field;
  5. inserts the serialized token at the captured caret or replaces the captured selection;
  6. returns focus to the source editor and reports the local change.

The modal does not write or rebuild the document. The source editor owns the buffer mutation and existing dirty-state workflow.

Catalogue Modal

The first modal contains:

  • one search across Work, Series, and Moment targets;
  • optional type filters for narrowing results after search begins;
  • result type, id, and distinguishing target-lookup projection fields;
  • the selected target type and id as the identity to insert;
  • a required Title field for this occurrence;
  • a short target-lookup summary or preview where declared;
  • Add catalogue token and Cancel actions.

Selected source text seeds the catalogue search and prefills Title, which remains editable. The author does not choose Work, Series, or Moment before searching. Result labels and lookup-projected context help decide what the selected words mean. For example, nerve may surface Work 00008 and Series 105.

Choosing a result establishes the pending target type and id. The author may compare and change results until confirming Add catalogue token. After insertion that concrete identity is immutable.

If there was no source selection, choosing a target prefills Title from its canonical title. Confirming a current lookup result and satisfying the declared required fields is the feature's only semantic validation gate. It guarantees what this modal inserts at this moment; it does not constrain later direct source editing or turn save/rebuild into document-wide validation.

Recognize A Token

Recognition runs against the current textarea buffer, including unsaved edits. It uses the accepted token grammar and parsed occurrence ranges, not a separate loose regular expression.

A collapsed caret activates a token only when it is strictly inside the token's outer opening and closing delimiters:

  • before the opening delimiter: no token;
  • inside the token definition: activate it;
  • after the closing delimiter: no token;
  • at the shared boundary between adjacent tokens: no token.

Malformed forms and token-like text in fenced or inline code do not activate a token. A user-selected range does not activate a token unless it is the exact range selected by the feature for the already-active occurrence.

Token Info View

The recognized family selects its corresponding hosted Info-panel view. The Catalogue view shows:

  • Family: Catalogue, read-only;
  • Target type: Work, Series, or Moment, read-only;
  • Target id: immutable and read-only;
  • declared target context when a lookup projection is available;
  • editable occurrence Title;
  • Update token and Remove token actions.

The view edits fields encoded in this occurrence. It does not edit the canonical target record. It cannot change target type or id. Re-targeting is deliberately Remove token, followed by Add catalogue token.

The Catalogue Info view has no catalogue search or replacement-target control. The resolved summary is context for the immutable identity, not a selectable result.

The view may present four field groups:

  • immutable identity;
  • editable occurrence fields parsed from the current buffer;
  • read-only attributes from the rebuilt usage index;
  • read-only target-lookup projections such as destinations or preview images.

Only fields declared as occurrence fields render editable controls. A simple new optional occurrence field can use a token-definition-declared supported control type. Usage-index attributes never override fields parsed from the current buffer and may be stale until rebuild. Canonical and derived target fields appear only when the active token-kind definition declares their lookup projections. The Info view reads that projection by immutable identity; it does not inspect the raw canonical record, traverse arrays such as Work files[], or infer additional fields. A Work preview image is lookup context, not occurrence data. If lookup context is unavailable, the view retains the identity and occurrence fields parsed from source without presenting the failure as a source validation result.

Each later family gets its own Info view through its own specification and delivery. Shared rendering may be extracted only after the fields and behavior are genuinely common.

Broken-Link Repair

The manage-only Docs Broken Links report is the repair entrypoint for an existing token that no longer resolves. A semantic-token issue row opens the owning document in source mode and should select the exact occurrence where the available source/range contract permits.

The author then removes the broken token and uses the family add modal to choose a current target. The Info view does not gain identity replacement controls for this workflow. Rebuild applies the repaired source and rerunning the audit confirms the issue is gone.

Highlight, Update, And Remove

Activating a token selects its exact source range in the existing textarea. That native selection is the first highlighting contract; the feature does not need a syntax-highlighting overlay or richer editor.

The active occurrence retains:

  • start and end offsets;
  • the raw token text;
  • a buffer revision or equivalent stale-range guard.

Before update or removal, the source editor confirms that the expected raw token still occupies the range. If not, it re-resolves the occurrence or cancels the action rather than mutating stale offsets.

Update token serializes the same immutable identity with the edited occurrence metadata and replaces only that exact range.

Remove token deletes only the token source. It does not remove adjacent whitespace or punctuation and it does not preserve or unwrap the displayed title. The change remains local and undoable through the normal editor until the document is rebuilt.

After either action, focus returns to the source editor, dirty state is projected normally, and the Info panel returns to ordinary source context unless another token is active.

Existing UI Reused In CT-P1

CT-P1 reuses:

  • the Markdown textarea and local dirty-state workflow;
  • the narrow active source-editor adapter;
  • title-weighted target search and keyboard-navigable result rows;
  • manage-only hosted Info-panel views;
  • the management action and modal lifecycle;
  • token construction and local selection replacement.

The mixed target search/results component now runs inside the Catalogue modal, and the hosted picker is removed. The caret-driven Catalogue Info view remains P2 work; source mode shows ordinary metadata information until then.

Refactoring Triggers

Call out and resolve these before the Catalogue UI is implemented:

  • If family actions require hardcoded branches in source-editor lifecycle code, add a focused contribution mechanism.
  • If target search/results cannot move out of the hosted picker without carrying Info-panel lifecycle or insertion ownership with them, separate the reusable result component from the pilot view first.
  • If the Info host cannot switch safely from ordinary source context to a family-specific view, extend its contextual view routing.
  • If the adapter cannot select or guarded-replace an arbitrary exact range, add those generic buffer operations without adding token knowledge to core.
  • If modal focus loses the original selection, capture selection text and range before opening.
  • If native textarea selection does not remain sufficiently visible while the Info view has focus, review a small active-range presentation enhancement before considering a richer editor.

Accessibility And Review

  • Toolbar and modal controls use the exact token-family name.
  • Identity and editable fields have visible labels; read-only identity is not presented as a disabled editable input.
  • Result selection supports keyboard navigation and announces target type, identity, and the selected catalogue item.
  • Modal cancellation makes no buffer change and returns focus predictably.
  • Caret boundaries, selection highlighting, update, removal, stale-range handling, and narrow/mobile Info-panel fit need manual UI review.
  • Permanent automated checks should protect parser/range behavior, adapter mutation contracts, required-field validation, and view registration rather than modal timing or visual choreography.
